name: Main Market Square
places: Adam Mickiewicz Monument, Main Market Square
description: The huge medieval square at the heart of the old town, with the Cloth Hall in the middle and a museum of the city’s past underneath.

name: St Mary’s Basilica
description: The brick Gothic church on the Main Market Square, with a carved wooden altarpiece and a trumpet call played from its tower every hour.

name: Central Square, Nowa Huta
description: The main square of Nowa Huta, the socialist-realist steel town built in the 1950s on the city’s eastern edge.

name: Oskar Schindler’s Enamel Factory
description: Oskar Schindler’s former factory, now a museum about life in Kraków under Nazi occupation from 1939 to 1945.

name: Piwnica pod Baranami
description: A cellar cabaret under a palace on the Main Market Square, running since 1956, with cabaret and jazz evenings.

name: Czartoryski Museum
description: A museum of art and historical objects collected by the Czartoryski family, including Leonardo da Vinci’s Lady with an Ermine.

name: Płaszów camp memorial
description: The site of the Nazi labour and concentration camp at Płaszów, now an open hillside with memorials to those who were held and killed there.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
description: A salt mine worked for about 700 years just outside Kraków, with chambers, chapels and statues carved from rock salt deep underground.

name: Wawel Cathedral
description: The royal cathedral on Wawel Hill, where Polish kings were crowned and buried. The great Sigismund Bell hangs in its tower.
